meta.title: Christianity vs Islam: better rules of warfare?
meta.thesis: Comparing scriptural norms, classical just-war / siyar traditions, and historical practice, which faith's warfare ethic better constrains violence and protects non-combatants?
meta.purpose: Steelman just war, crusading history, Qur'anic jihad limits, and classical offensive jihad. Separate Jesus' personal ethic, Christendom law, Muhammad as statesman, and modern misuse.
meta.warning: Define the comparison class: Jesus' sayings vs Muhammad's campaigns? Aquinas vs al-Shaybani? Modern catechism vs ISIS proof-texts? Mixing levels is how both sides cheat.

definitions.term: Just war (ius ad bellum / in bello)
definitions.precise: Western Christian-derived criteria for when war may be started and how it must be fought (legitimate authority, just cause, proportionality, discrimination, etc.).
definitions.not: Not identical with everything done by Christian empires.

definitions.precise: Struggle; in law often includes armed jihad with rules (siyar). Must specify defensive, offensive, spiritual, or polemical misuse.
definitions.not: Not a synonym for terrorism or for any Muslim violence.

definitions.precise: Norm against intentionally targeting civilians, women, children, clergy, etc.
definitions.not: Not the same as zero collateral damage in siege warfare.

definitions.precise: Claim that later Medinan fighting verses supersede earlier restraint — contested in scope among Muslim scholars.
definitions.not: Do not assume one popular 'sword verse abrogates all peace' meme settles fiqh.

definitions.precise: Distinguish the Sermon on the Mount's personal enemy-love from later Christian political theology authorizing force.
definitions.not: Christians may not hide crusade history behind Matthew 5 without argument.

definitions.precise: Islamic international/military law genre (e.g. Shaybani) regulating war and peace.
definitions.not: Not identical with every raid narrative in the sīrah.

arguments.title: Jesus' enemy-love sets a higher bar than armed prophethood

christian.claim: The founder forbids retaliatory violence and loves enemies (Matt 5:38–48); Muhammad leads battles. The founding pattern favors Christianity.
christian.case: Matthew 26:52; John 18:36. Even when Christians later just-war theorize, the canonical center is non-vengeance. Comparative ethics starts with the founder.

quotes.text: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
Put your sword back into its place; for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.

data_points.fact: Jesus' kingdom is 'not from this world' (John 18:36) — Christian readings split on whether that bans all state violence.
data_points.label: Jesus' kingdom is 'not from this world' (John 18:36) — Christian readings split on whether that bans all state violence.

muslim.claim: Jesus' ethic addresses personal disciples under occupation; Muhammad receives rules for a polity facing war. Different roles, not moral failure — and OT holy war complicates Christian claims.
muslim.case: Qur'an 22:39–40 permission to fight when expelled; 2:190 non-transgression. Luke 22:36 and OT conquest narratives show biblical tradition is not pacifist-only.

quotes.text: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged.

data_points.fact: Romans 13 and Luke 22:36 are used to show the NT is not simple pacifism.
data_points.label: Romans 13 and Luke 22:36 are used to show the NT is not simple pacifism.

data_points.fact: A prophet with political authority faces questions Jesus, in the Gospels, does not — apples to oranges unless you compare Constantine/just war to siyar.
data_points.label: A prophet with political authority faces questions Jesus, in the Gospels, does not — apples to oranges unless you compare Constantine/just war to siyar.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Selective pacifism: ignore Joshua, Samuel, Revelation warfare imagery, and church history.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: If roles differ, say so — but then don't claim moral equivalence of founding examples without argument.
arguments.crux: Is the morally decisive datum the founder's personal violence profile or the mature legal ethic of each tradition?
arguments.debate_use: Force agreement on comparison class before scoring 'better.'
arguments.why_it_matters: Highest Christian moral altitude claim. If it is the ethic, armed prophethood looks like a downgrade. If it is interim pacifism, the NT church's later just war is the real comparator.

live.if_they_say: Jesus never fought, so Christianity is the peace religion.
live.you_say: Jesus' personal nonviolence is real. Then ask what Christians did with armies for 1700 years, and whether the fair Islamic comparator is Muhammad in Medina or a village Sufi. Match offices: preacher vs statesman, or church vs umma.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't erase Crusades. Don't erase Maghāzī.

arguments.title: Qur'anic fighting is primarily defensive and limited

christian.claim: 9:5, 9:29, 8:39 and classical offensive jihad show expansionist religious war is structural, not a modern distortion.
christian.case: Sword-verse rhetoric in apologetics; Maghāzī literature; classical manuals on inviting then fighting unbelievers. 'Religion of peace' overclaims fail against sources.

sources.label: EJIL — Use of Force under Islamic Law

quotes.text: And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them…
Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day… from those who were given the Book, until they give the jizya willingly while they are humbled.
quotes.work: People of the Book fighting verse

muslim.claim: Core permissions answer persecution and treaty-breaking; 2:190 and non-combatant hadiths constrain excess; extremist readings violate classical limits.
muslim.case: Tafsir tying 9:5 to specific hostile polytheist groups after pilgrimage season; hadith forbidding killing women/children. Modern Muslim majorities reject ISIS proof-texting.

quotes.text: Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
There is no compulsion in religion.

data_points.fact: Asbāb al-nuzūl for 9:5 typically tie it to treaty-breaking pagans, not a timeless 'kill all unbelievers' license — fight the tafsīr, don't ignore 9:5.
data_points.label: Asbāb al-nuzūl for 9:5 typically tie it to treaty-breaking pagans, not a timeless 'kill all unbelievers' license — fight the tafsīr, don't ignore 9:5.

data_points.fact: Reuven Firestone and others: Qur'anic war verses are historically layered, not a single slogan.
data_points.source: Firestone, Jihad: The Origin of Holy War in Islam
data_points.label: Reuven Firestone and others: Qur'anic war verses are historically layered, not a single slogan.
data_points.note: Firestone, Jihad: The Origin of Holy War in Islam

arguments.counter_to_christian: Quoting 9:5 without asbāb al-nuzūl and without 9:6 safe-conduct is proof-text abuse.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Classical offensive jihad theories exist; 'only defensive' is not the whole heritage.
arguments.crux: Do Medinan war verses authorize enduring offensive holy war or context-bound defense under limits?
arguments.debate_use: Put 2:190 and 9:5 side by side; demand a reconciliation theory from both.
arguments.why_it_matters: Street slogan vs 9:5/9:29. Definitions of 'defensive' decide the round.

counters.claim: Islam's last word is 'kill the polytheists.'
counters.reply: Read 9:4–7 (treaty-keepers excepted) and 2:190. Then compare herem texts in Joshua. Isolation is a method both sides abuse.

live.you_say: Abrogation is a real classical theory — don't deny it. Then ask which legal school, whether 9:5 is bound to ḥudaybiya-breakers, and what 9:6 (granting asylum) is doing in the same passage.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't pretend 9:5 is a greeting-card. Don't pretend 2:256 deleted 9:29 from fiqh.

arguments.title: Non-combatant protections

christian.claim: Just-war discrimination and modern Christian teaching (e.g. CCC) clearly forbid targeting civilians; Islamic sources include harsher siege/slavery outcomes in practice.
christian.case: Aquinas ST II-II; CCC 2302–2317. Christians argue their mature doctrine aligns with Geneva-like norms more cleanly.

quotes.text: Augustine and later Aquinas distinguish just cause from right conduct (jus ad bellum / jus in bello).

muslim.claim: Prophetic instructions forbid killing women, children, and often monks/hermits; mutilation and treachery banned — a robust in-bello ethic early in history.
muslim.case: Abu Bakr's reported directives; hadith collections on non-killing of non-combatants. Christendom's massacres (Jerusalem 1099 etc.) undercut moral superiority narratives.

quotes.text: Do not kill a woman, nor a child, nor an old man, nor cut down fruit trees…
quotes.who: Abū Bakr's reported instructions to armies (standard siyar citation)
quotes.work: Transmitted in siyar / tārīkh collections; wording varies by report

data_points.fact: Prophetic hadith against killing women and children in combat is a mainstream siyar building block.
data_points.label: Prophetic hadith against killing women and children in combat is a mainstream siyar building block.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Crusades, wars of religion, and colonial violence are part of the Christian record.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Siege practice, enslavement of captives, and some ridda/khawārij treatments complicate the soft reading.
arguments.crux: Whose official norms better protect civilians — and how much do historical crimes discount the norms?
arguments.debate_use: Score norms and history on separate ballots.
arguments.why_it_matters: Conduct of war is where both traditions have usable law and ugly history.

live.you_say: Siyar texts do. Then both of you have to survive your own history: Maghāzī raids, Crusader massacres, 20th-c. bombing. Law on the page vs practice is the shared human problem.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't cite ISIS as 'the' fiqh. Don't cite a just-war manual as 'the' Crusades.

arguments.title: Just war vs siyar as legal achievements

christian.claim: Augustine–Aquinas–Vitoria–Grotius trajectory developed criteria that shaped modern international law; that is a major moral-intellectual achievement.
christian.case: Legitimate authority, just cause, right intention, last resort, proportionality. Muslims may parallel this, but Christian genealogy of ius gentium is historically central.

muslim.claim: Siyar developed rules of treaties, safe-conduct (amān), and categories of combatants centuries before Westphalia; Islamic law is not a late borrower of restraint.
muslim.case: Shaybani's Siyar; amān in 9:6; treaty of Hudaybiyya as precedent. Comparative legal history is not a Christian monopoly.

sources.label: Khadduri, The Islamic Law of Nations

data_points.fact: Majid Khadduri's translation of Shaybānī is the usual English gateway to classical siyar.
data_points.label: Majid Khadduri's translation of Shaybānī is the usual English gateway to classical siyar.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Just war also rationalized conquest; genealogy ≠ moral purity.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Classical dār al-Islām / dār al-ḥarb frames can encode permanent hostility.
arguments.crux: Which legal tradition better institutionalizes restraint as law rather than as piety alone?
arguments.debate_use: Compare Aquinas article and a siyar ruling side by side on civilian targeting.
arguments.why_it_matters: Adult comparison: Aquinas vs Shaybānī, not Jesus-the-pacifist vs a YouTube clip of 9:5.

live.you_say: Just-war vocabulary is Latin-Christian. Limitation-of-war as law is not unique. Compare Shaybānī and Aquinas on cause, authority, and noncombatants — then score.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't baptize either tradition as the Geneva Conventions.

arguments.title: Religious coercion adjacent to warfare ethics

christian.claim: NT lacks a death penalty for apostasy; classical ridda law and blasphemy violence worsen Islam's overall force-ethic score.
christian.case: Bukhari 6922 vs John 6:66–67 freedom to walk away. Even if war rules are comparable, internal coercion matters.

data_points.fact: Deut 13 and later Christendom's heresy laws are the Christian skeleton in this closet.
data_points.label: Deut 13 and later Christendom's heresy laws are the Christian skeleton in this closet.

muslim.claim: 2:256 no compulsion; many modern scholars reject capital apostasy for private belief; Christian history of heresy executions undercuts uniqueness claims.
muslim.case: Ridda wars read as political rebellion; Inquisition/heresy laws show Christian polities also fused religion and lethal force.

data_points.fact: Classical ridda/hiraba and sabb al-rasūl rulings are the Islamic skeleton.
data_points.label: Classical ridda/hiraba and sabb al-rasūl rulings are the Islamic skeleton.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Christendom enforced orthodoxy with violence for centuries.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Reformist rejection of apostasy death is not identical with classical consensus.
arguments.crux: Should warfare ethics scoring include domestic religious coercion laws?
arguments.debate_use: If motion is 'rules of warfare,' park apostasy unless opponent opens it.
arguments.why_it_matters: Where warfare ethics bleeds into liberty of conscience.

live.you_say: Classical fiqh often does prescribe death for apostasy. Christian history often did too. The live question is which scriptures still authorize it as a religious good, and who reformed.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't pretend all Muslim states apply hudud. Don't pretend the Inquisition is a cartoon with no bodies.

arguments.title: Old Testament ḥērem vs Qur'anic jihad

christian.claim: OT ḥērem is covenantal-historical and not the church's marching orders; the NT reframes enemy treatment. Islam's war texts remain operative law in classical fiqh.
christian.case: Hermeneutical discontinuity: Joshua ≠ Jesus' mission. Muslim abrogation theories keep fighting verses live in a way Christian supersession of ḥērem does not.

quotes.text: They devoted to destruction by the edge of the sword all in the city, both men and women, young and old, oxen, sheep, and donkeys.

muslim.claim: If Christians own the whole Bible, ḥērem is harsher than Qur'anic rules; special pleading about 'that was then' must be available to Muslims too.
muslim.case: 1 Samuel 15; Deut 20. Comparative scripture ethics cannot baptize OT violence while essentializing Qur'an 9.

data_points.fact: If OT ḥērem is 'old covenant,' say what moral rule makes Qur'anic jihad still live while Joshua is dead.
data_points.label: If OT ḥērem is 'old covenant,' say what moral rule makes Qur'anic jihad still live while Joshua is dead.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Marcionism is heresy — the OT remains Christian scripture.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Symmetry requires Muslims to allow Christian progressive revelation arguments.
arguments.crux: May each side restrict operative war ethics to later revelation/hermeneutics?
arguments.debate_use: Demand parallel hermeneutical rules before comparing bloodiest texts.
arguments.why_it_matters: Best Muslim tu quoque. Christians must have a theology of herem, not a memory-hole.

live.you_say: Open Joshua 6 and 1 Samuel 15. Then discuss covenant, typology, and whether Muhammad's wars look more like Joshua, like David, or like Augustine. Isolation is not a method.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't say Joshua didn't happen as a moral free pass. Don't say 9:5 is just like a psalm of lament.

arguments.title: Crusades, colonialism, and Maghāzī

christian.claim: Crusades are often politically complex and not simple 'kill all Muslims' doctrine; Islamic conquests and slave-raiding likewise. Founder-level ethics still differ.
christian.case: Acknowledge sins of Christendom while arguing they violate Jesus more clearly than expansionist jihad violates Muhammad's model.

sources.label: CCC on peace / unjust war themes

muslim.claim: Crusader massacres and later colonial wars under Christian symbols destroy claims of uniquely peaceful Christian civilization.
muslim.case: Jerusalem 1099 narratives; Reconquista; modern wars. Moral scoreboards that ignore Christian violence are apologetic, not historical.

arguments.counter_to_christian: If practice can indict Islam, it can indict Christianity.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: If practice can indict Christianity, cite Islamic conquest violence too.
arguments.crux: Do historical crimes refute a tradition's rules, or only its faithfulness?
arguments.debate_use: Propose: norms 50%, founder 30%, civilizational practice 20% — then argue weights.
arguments.why_it_matters: History dump round. Force a metric: founding texts vs later empires.

live.you_say: Those are Christian-world crimes. Maghāzī, ridda, futūḥ, and later sultanates are Muslim-world wars. Score founders, classical law, and modern outcomes separately or you are just trading body counts.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't excuse atrocity as 'context' only for your side.

arguments.title: Prisoners, spoils, and slavery in war

christian.claim: Regulating slavery and sex with captives (e.g. debates on mā malakat aymānukum) is a moral deficit relative to Gospel trajectory toward liberation.
christian.case: Qur'an 33:50; 4:24 debates; classical fiqh on captives. Christians argue NT seedbed abolishes the category over time more cleanly.

muslim.claim: Islam regulated and incentivized manumission in a slave economy universal to late antiquity; Christian canon also assumes slavery (Eph 6; Col 3).
muslim.case: 90:13; 24:33. Comparative ancient ethics: both inherit slavery; Islam's war-captive rules are of their time, not uniquely evil.

quotes.text: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them]…

arguments.counter_to_christian: Christian slaveholding lasted into modernity with biblical defense.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Regulation is not abolition; moral progress claims need clear trajectory.
arguments.crux: Is regulating war-captive slavery better, worse, or equal to NT household codes?
arguments.debate_use: Keep this argument from swallowing the whole warfare motion — timebox it.
arguments.why_it_matters: Q 47:4, 8:41, 33:50 vs NT silence / later church practice.

live.you_say: 8:41 and 4:24 are in the book — grant the texts. Then compare OT spoils (Num 31) and Christian just-war ransom practice. The distinctive Islamic fight is whether those rules remain exemplary.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't deny the verses. Don't pretend medieval Christians had clean hands on captives.

arguments.title: Modern terrorism and proof-texting

christian.claim: Jihadist groups cite mainstream-accessible texts; the recurrence suggests a textual vulnerability Christianity's NT center lacks.
christian.case: 9:5/9:29 in extremist literature. Christian terrorists usually contradict Jesus more blatantly.

data_points.fact: Graeme Wood's ISIS analysis: they were following a coherent extreme reading, not 'no Islam.'
data_points.source: Wood, What ISIS Really Wants / The Way of the Strangers
data_points.label: Graeme Wood's ISIS analysis: they were following a coherent extreme reading, not 'no Islam.'
data_points.note: Wood, What ISIS Really Wants / The Way of the Strangers

muslim.claim: Takfīrī terrorism violates siyar, targets civilians, and is condemned by mainstream scholars; guilt by extremist citation is like blaming Jesus for KKK misuse of the Bible.
muslim.case: Open letters against ISIS; classical conditions for jihad (authority, non-combatant rules). Method: misuse ≠ meaning.

data_points.fact: Mainstream fiqh: targeting civilians, breaking oaths, and indiscriminate takfir are ḥarām; Khawārij are the classical warning tale.
data_points.source: Classical ḥudūd / siyar + modern marājiʿ statements
data_points.label: Mainstream fiqh: targeting civilians, breaking oaths, and indiscriminate takfir are ḥarām; Khawārij are the classical warning tale.
data_points.note: Classical ḥudūd / siyar + modern marājiʿ statements

arguments.counter_to_christian: Christian nationalist violence and crusader romanticism also cite scripture.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: If mainstream classical law includes offensive jihad, 'extremist only' is incomplete.
arguments.crux: Are jihadist readings parasitic distortions or one authentic classical option?
arguments.debate_use: Ask for named madhhab positions, not only Twitter scholars.
arguments.why_it_matters: Modern audiences start here. You still need a text-to-practice map.

live.you_say: They cited Islamic texts. So did their Muslim enemies. The adult move is: which reading is central vs extreme, and what does the same method do to Christian Reconstructionist violence.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't say 'nothing to do with Islam.' Don't say 'this is all Muslims.'

arguments.title: Treaties, reciprocity, and proportionality

christian.claim: Gospel enemy-love and just-war last resort/proportionality give a clearer path to stable peace than expansionist jihad frames.
christian.case: Romans 12:17–21; just-war manuals. Peace is not merely temporary hudna pending strength.

data_points.fact: Pacta sunt servanda in just-war and in Grotius sits in a Christian-European legal story.
data_points.label: Pacta sunt servanda in just-war and in Grotius sits in a Christian-European legal story.

muslim.claim: Qur'an commands fulfillment of covenants (9:4; 16:91) and incline to peace if enemy inclines (8:61); Hudaybiyya shows strategic peacemaking.
muslim.case: Treaty ethics are central. 8:61 is a high-water mark for reciprocal de-escalation.

quotes.text: Excepted are those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists and they have not been deficient toward you… so fulfill their treaty to its term.

arguments.counter_to_christian: Christian states broke treaties constantly; norms ≠ compliance.
arguments.counter_to_muslim: Debates on whether 8:61 is abrogated by later sūrah 9 must be faced honestly.
arguments.crux: Is peace a stable end-state in each ethic, or a pause in religious struggle?
arguments.debate_use: Ask both: name conditions for ending war permanently with a non-co-religionist state.
arguments.why_it_matters: Where both can sound like Geneva — and both can be accused of bad faith.

live.if_they_say: Muslims may break any treaty with unbelievers.
live.you_say: 9:4 and 8:72 and the Constitution of Medina tradition cut against that slogan. Then discuss Hudaybiyyah and whether 'no compulsion' survives conquest. Slogans both ways are lazy.
live.dont_overclaim: Don't ignore 9:1–15's treaty-break frame. Don't ignore Christian colonial treaty-breaking.

debates.title: Islam and violence debates (Wood / Ally pattern)
debates.motion: Is Islam a religion of peace / how violent are the sources?
debates.summary: Wood stacks Medinan war texts and sīrah; Ally stresses context, defensive reading, and Christian violence history.
what_to_steal: Bring OT ḥērem when sword verses appear

opponent_cards.trigger: Islam is a religion of peace — period
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Ask which texts and which legal school. Peaceful Muslims ≠ settled classical doctrine on offensive jihad.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Offer: many verses command restraint — and some authorize fighting. Both are in the sources.

opponent_cards.trigger: Kill the pagans wherever you find them (9:5)
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Context: specific treaty-breakers after sacred months; 9:6 grants protection if they seek it. Still debate scope — but not a cartoon.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask if they apply the same literal forever-reading to Deut 20.

opponent_cards.trigger: Jesus said turn the other cheek, so Christianity wins
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Personal ethic vs state ethic. Ask about just war, soldiers in NT, and OT. Comparison class matters.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Grant the Sermon's radicalness; then ask how Christian empires should be scored.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: Crimes count against practice. They don't automatically make Qur'anic war rules gentler. Score both.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask for Islamic conquest counter-examples they accept as parallel.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: Greater/lesser jihad rhetoric exists, but fiqh books regulate armed jihad extensively. Don't erase that.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Define which sense is used in tonight's motion.

opponent_cards.trigger: Muhammad was a warlord, not a prophet
opponent_cards.fast_answer: That's a conclusion. First compare roles: Jesus non-state teacher vs Moses/David-like lawgiver-leader.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask if Moses fails the same test.

opponent_cards.trigger: Just war is just Christian spin for violence
opponent_cards.fast_answer: It can be abused. It also supplies criteria to condemn abusive wars — including Christian ones.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Ask which criterion they reject: discrimination? proportionality?

opponent_cards.trigger: Muslims must fight until all religion is for Allah (8:39)
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Exegetes dispute whether this means end persecution/fitnah or global forced conversion. Force a tafsir.

opponent_cards.trigger: Christianity caused more deaths in history
opponent_cards.fast_answer: Body-count debates depend on centuries, technology, and demography. Prefer norms + founder + representative law.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Refuse unfalsifiable genocide Olympics unless data standards are set.

opponent_cards.fast_answer: They claim to. Mainstream Open Letter and classical non-combatant rules say they don't. Ask for your opponent's usūl.
opponent_cards.follow_up: Still press classical offensive jihad if that's the real target.

checklist: Lock comparison class: founder / scripture / classical law / modern teaching
Prepare 60-second definitions: just war, jihad, non-combatant, abrogation
Prepare OT ḥērem symmetry move and Christian discontinuity reply
Separate in bello rules from ad bellum expansion questions
Decide concessions: Crusades; classical offensive jihad
Drill 10 opponent cards; first line live-ready
Bring Aquinas Q.40 + one siyar/EJIL receipt
Score norms and history separately in closing
No slogan closings: 'religion of peace' or 'Jesus vs warlord' without crux
Timebox slavery/apostasy digressions unless motion includes them
Ask opponent to state conditions for permanent peace with the other faith's polity

Christian podium: Founder's enemy-love and rejection of sword-retaliation is a unique moral center
Just-war criteria (discrimination, proportionality, last resort) are a high legal achievement
NT lacks an apostolic program of religious conquest
Medinan expansionist texts and classical offensive jihad are structural challenges for Islam
Muslim podium: Early, explicit non-combatant protections and amān/treaty ethics
Permission to fight answers persecution; 2:190 and 8:61 constrain aggression
Siyar is a mature laws-of-war tradition, not chaos
Christian scripture and history contain ḥērem, crusade, and holy-war practice — no innocence narrative
Unity / steelman: Both traditions contain restraint norms and violent chapters — punish proof-texting
Agree on comparison class before scoring
Condemn civilian-targeting terrorism as betrayal of the best in both
Use legal classics (Aquinas, siyar) not only atrocity headlines
